'''Benjamin Michael Zuckerman''' (born August 16, 1943) is an American [[astrophysicist]] and [[Environmentalism|environmentalist]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ricci |first=James |date=2002-06-09 |title=The Sierra Club and the Immigration Freight Train |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-jun-09-tm-45400-story.html |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> and an emeritus professor in the Department of Physics & Astronomy at [[UCLA]].<ref name="google">{{cite book|title=Reports of the President and the Treasurer - John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|author=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|date=1976|publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation.|issn=0190-227X|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7Q80AAAAIAAJ|access-date=2015-04-10}}</ref> His recent work focusses primarily on the formation and evolution of [[planetary systems]] around various types of [[stars]]. Zuckerman was a member of the board of directors of the [[Sierra Club]] from 2002 to 2005<ref>{{Cite web |title=Roster of Sierra Club Directors |url=https://www.sierraclub.org/sites/default/files/2026-06/roster-of-sierra-club-directors-2026.pdf |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Sierra Club}}</ref> and the [[Sea Shepherd Conservation Society]] from 2002 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Camilla |date=1 March 2016 |title=Professor emeritus narrows space between astronomy, environmentalism |url=https://dailybruin.com/2016/03/01/professor-emeritus-narrows-space-between-astronomy-environmentalism/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Daily Bruin}}</ref> He was an advocate for U.S. population stabilization, demonstrated by his co-founding of the internal Sierra Club group Sierrans for U.S. Population Stabilization and his Presidency of the non-profit organization [[Californians for Population Stabilization]] (CAPS) until its merger with [[NumbersUSA]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-12 |title=California anti-immigrant group CAPS merges with NumbersUSA |url=https://www.splcenter.org/resources/hatewatch/california-anti-immigrant-groups-caps-numbersusa-merge/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Southern Poverty Law Center |language=en-US}}</ref> Both groups argued for immigration and fertility levels that would enable the U.S. population to stabilize, thereby helping to protect the U.S. environment. 

== Education ==
Zuckerman completed two degrees in 1963, one in Physics and one in Aeronautic & Astronautics at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. He finished his PhD thesis in Astronomy in 1968 at [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://astro.ucla.edu/personnel/benjamin-zuckerman |title=Benjamin Zuckerman webpage on UCLA Department of Physics and Astronomy website. |access-date=2015-12-26 |archive-date=2015-12-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227024443/http://astro.ucla.edu/personnel/benjamin-zuckerman |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Publications ==
Since 1965, Zuckerman has published well over 200 refereed papers in journals such as ''[[Astrophysical Journal]]'', ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', ''[[Astronomy & Astrophysics]]'' and ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''.<ref>Benjamin Zuckerman publication list on [http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abstract_service.html NASA ADS]</ref> He also produced a number of review papers in the ''[[Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics]]''. In 2001, he contributed to the ''Encyclopedia of Astronomy and Astrophysics''.<ref name="Zuckerman2001">{{cite encyclopedia |last=Zuckerman|first=Benjamin|chapter=Dusty Circumstellar Disks|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Astronomy and Astrophysics|year=2001|doi=10.1888/0333750888/1845|bibcode=2001eaa..bookE1845Z|isbn=0-333-75088-8}} {{cite web |url=http://eaa.crcpress.com/ |title=Encyclopedia of Astronomy and Astrophysics |access-date=2009-08-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141122121344/http://eaa.crcpress.com/ |archive-date=2014-11-22 }}</ref>

Zuckerman was co-author of a 2008 paper reporting first directly imaged multiplanetary system (arguably, the first directly imaged planets) around [[HR 8799]]<ref name="Marois2008">{{cite journal |last=Marois |first=Christian |display-authors=etal |date=November 2008 |title=Direct Imaging of Multiple Planets Orbiting the Star HR 8799 |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=322 |issue=5906 |pages=1348–1352 |doi=10.1126/science.1166585 |arxiv=0811.2606 |pmid=19008415 |bibcode=2008Sci...322.1348M|s2cid=206516630 }}</ref> and a 2010 paper discovering a fourth imaged planet in the system: [[HR 8799 e]].<ref name=Marois2010>{{Cite journal |last1=Marois |first1=C. |last2=Zuckerman |first2=B. |last3=Konopacky |first3=Q. M. |last4=MacIntosh |first4=B. |last5=Barman |first5=T. |title=Images of a fourth planet orbiting HR 8799 |doi=10.1038/nature09684 |journal=Nature |volume=468 |issue=7327 |pages=1080–1083 |year=2010 |pmid=21150902 |arxiv=1011.4918 |bibcode=2010Natur.468.1080M|s2cid=4425891 }}</ref>

In 1982 Zuckerman co-edited the book ''Extraterrestrials, Where Are They?'' with [[Michael H. Hart|Michael Hart]], a known [[White nationalism|white nationalist]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-04-19 |title=Californians for Population Stabilization Board Chair Ben Zuckerman Co-Edited Book with White Nationalist |url=https://www.splcenter.org/resources/hatewatch/californians-population-stabilization-board-chair-ben-zuckerman-co-edited-book-white/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Southern Poverty Law Center |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>[[Google Books]] link to the [https://books.google.com/books/about/Extraterrestrials_where_are_they.html?id=2uwzAAAAIAAJ 1995 2nd edition of the book]</ref> In 1996 he also co-authored the book ''The Origin and Evolution of the Universe'' with Matthew A. Malkan and co-edited the book ''Human Population and the Environmental Crisis'' with David Jefferson, following a public symposium of the same name held at UCLA in October 1993.<ref>[http://www.abebooks.fr/9780867209662/Human-Population-Environmental-Crisis-Zuckerman-0867209666/plp Description of the book] on [[AbeBooks]] website.</ref>
